summary_for_david.description: Three sentences for a product owner who cannot read code: what this round was about, whether anything should worry him, and the one thing worth his attention.

what_happened.description: The round in plain English, finding by finding: what the reviewer was worried about in terms of outcomes, what the builder did about it, and whether the diff bears that out. Prose, in whatever shape reads best.

disagreements.description: Where your reading of the round differs from the builder's account. An empty array is a real answer; never pad it and never suppress an item.

what.description: What the builder's account says, and what you think instead.

why_it_matters.description: What it would mean for David or for the work if you are right.

took_on_trust.description: What you accepted from the builder without checking it yourself, and why. Almost never empty. Distinct from could_not_assess: this is what you SAW and did not independently verify, not what you could not reach. Does not set the 'partial' signal.

could_not_assess.description: One sentence when something in this round was beyond what you could REACH -- a diff too large, a thread you could not fetch, a finding you did not follow. null when there is no such thing. Not for hedging: David is told 'partial' rather than 'agrees' whenever this is set.

recommendation.description: One line: what, if anything, David should do.

model.description: The model id you are actually running as, read from your own context -- not the one you were asked to be. The dispatch can no longer observe this, so it is shown to David exactly as reported. If you cannot determine it, say so in words rather than guessing.

known_gaps.description: FINAL ROUND ONLY, omitted otherwise. What is shipping unfixed: declines that HELD (the reviewer did not raise the class again) plus any recorded-gaps table in the PR description. An empty array on a final round means nothing is shipping unfixed, which is a real answer.

what.description: What is shipping unfixed, in terms of what could happen rather than what the code does.

reasonable.description: Whether you think shipping it is reasonable.

why.description: Why you think that. Say plainly when you disagree with the decline -- this is the last moment anyone looks at it.

what_landed.description: FINAL ROUND ONLY, omitted otherwise. The PR description's stated intent held against what the diff actually does -- a comparison, never a restatement.

landed.description: What the change actually does, read from the diff.

does_not_do.description: What it does NOT do that David might assume it does, given how it was described.

now_trusting.description: What David is now trusting that he was not trusting before this change.
